definition: A technology that creates an encrypted tunnel between your device and a remote server, masking your IP address and encrypting internet traffic.
metaDescription: Learn what a VPN is, how it works, and why it matters for your online privacy and security.
simpleExplanation: A VPN is like a private, encrypted tunnel for your internet traffic. Your data travels through this tunnel to a VPN server first, hiding your real location.
whyItMatters: Without a VPN, your ISP can see every website you visit, hackers on public Wi-Fi can intercept your data, and websites can track your real location.
technicalDetail: VPNs use protocols like WireGuard, OpenVPN, or IKEv2 to establish encrypted tunnels. Traffic is encrypted on your device, sent to the VPN server, decrypted, and forwarded.

examples.explanation: A VPN encrypts all your data on coffee shop Wi-Fi, preventing other users from intercepting your passwords.
Your ISP normally logs every website you visit. With a VPN, they only see encrypted traffic to the VPN server.
